Risk Scenario: Unauthorized access could expose or modify sensitive patient information
Proposed Treatment Actions: Review database roles; remove excessive permissions; implement least privilege; schedule periodic access reviews; investigate privileged access
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.15 Access control; A.5.18 Access rights; A.8.3 Information access restriction"
Required Evidence: Approved access matrix; dated access-review record; database role export; remediation tickets
Success Criteria: All database permissions have an approved business owner and excessive access is removed

Risk Scenario: Exploitation of unpatched software could compromise customer information or service integrity
Proposed Treatment Actions: Establish vulnerability scanning cadence; triage findings by severity and exposure; apply security patches; retest fixes; document exceptions
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.8.8 Management of technical vulnerabilities; A.8.9 Configuration management; A.8.29 Security testing in development and acceptance"
Required Evidence: Authenticated scan report; patch records; remediation tickets; retest results; approved exception records
Success Criteria: Critical and high findings are remediated within approved timelines or formally risk-accepted

Risk Scenario: Incorrect storage permissions could expose medical documents to unauthorized parties
Proposed Treatment Actions: Review storage access policies; block public access unless explicitly approved; apply least privilege; enable access logging; test permissions
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.15 Access control; A.8.3 Information access restriction; A.8.12 Data leakage prevention; A.8.15 Logging"
Required Evidence: Storage policy export; public-access configuration; access-review approval; sample access logs; test results
Success Criteria: No unapproved public access exists and access is limited to authorized identities

Risk Scenario: Lost or compromised laptops could expose company information or credentials
Proposed Treatment Actions: Define endpoint security baseline; enforce full-disk encryption and endpoint protection; enable device lock and remote wipe where supported; track non-compliant devices
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.6.7 Remote working; A.7.9 Security of assets off-premises; A.8.1 User endpoint devices; A.8.7 Protection against malware"
Required Evidence: Device compliance report; encryption status export; endpoint protection console report; exception register; sample remote-wipe procedure
Success Criteria: All in-scope laptops meet the approved baseline or have documented exceptions and compensating controls

Risk Scenario: Compromised accounts could expose email and business documents
Proposed Treatment Actions: Review authentication policies; enforce MFA for users and administrators; disable legacy authentication where feasible; review risky sign-ins and privileged roles
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.16 Identity management; A.5.17 Authentication information; A.5.18 Access rights; A.8.5 Secure authentication"
Required Evidence: Tenant authentication policy export; MFA registration and enforcement report; legacy-authentication review; privileged-role review; sign-in alert samples
Success Criteria: MFA and approved authentication controls are enforced for in-scope accounts; exceptions are approved and tracked

Risk Scenario: Unauthorized repository access could expose proprietary code or introduce malicious changes
Proposed Treatment Actions: Restrict repository access to named users and teams; require MFA; protect main branches; review external collaborators; scan repositories for exposed secrets and rotate any confirmed exposed credentials
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.15 Access control; A.5.18 Access rights; A.8.4 Access to source code; A.8.25 Secure development life cycle; A.8.28 Secure coding"
Required Evidence: Repository permission export; branch-protection settings; collaborator review; secret-scan results; credential-rotation tickets
Success Criteria: Repository access is approved, sensitive branches are protected, and detected exposed secrets are revoked or rotated

Risk Scenario: Incorrect firewall rules could permit unauthorized network access
Proposed Treatment Actions: Review firewall rules against documented business requirements; remove stale or overly broad rules; restrict administrative access; log configuration changes; schedule periodic rule reviews
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.8.20 Network security; A.8.21 Security of network services; A.8.22 Segregation of networks; A.8.9 Configuration management"
Required Evidence: Approved firewall rulebase; rule-review sign-off; change tickets; configuration backup; sample firewall logs
Success Criteria: Every active rule has a documented purpose and owner; unnecessary rules are removed or formally excepted

Risk Scenario: An attacker could compromise production systems and backups
Proposed Treatment Actions: Separate backup administration from production administration; enable immutable or offline backup copies where supported; restrict deletion privileges; monitor backup jobs; perform restore tests
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.15 Access control; A.8.13 Information backup; A.8.14 Redundancy of information processing facilities; A.8.16 Monitoring activities"
Required Evidence: Backup architecture; immutability or offline-copy configuration; backup-job reports; privileged access review; restoration test report
Success Criteria: Protected backup copies exist, deletion is restricted and a restoration test meets approved recovery requirements

Risk Scenario: Former employees could retain unauthorized access if accounts are not disabled promptly
Proposed Treatment Actions: Define joiner-mover-leaver workflow; require HR notification of termination and role changes; disable accounts and revoke sessions promptly; reconcile active accounts to HR records
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.16 Identity management; A.5.18 Access rights; A.6.5 Responsibilities after termination or change of employment"
Required Evidence: Approved joiner-mover-leaver procedure; sample termination tickets; account-disable timestamps; HR-to-directory reconciliation
Success Criteria: Leaver access is removed within the approved SLA and exceptions are recorded and escalated

Risk Scenario: Service disruption could prevent clinics from accessing the platform
Proposed Treatment Actions: Define availability and capacity thresholds; monitor service health; conduct load and resilience testing; document incident escalation and customer communication; track capacity-related incidents
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.30 ICT readiness for business continuity; A.8.6 Capacity management; A.8.14 Redundancy of information processing facilities; A.8.16 Monitoring activities"
Required Evidence: Service-level objectives; monitoring dashboards; load-test report; incident records; capacity review
Success Criteria: Service capacity is monitored against approved thresholds and resilience weaknesses have tracked actions

Risk Scenario: Identity service compromise could enable access to multiple company systems
Proposed Treatment Actions: Harden identity-provider configuration; enforce MFA and conditional access where available; restrict and monitor privileged identity roles; review federation and recovery settings; test account-recovery controls
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.16 Identity management; A.5.17 Authentication information; A.8.2 Privileged access rights; A.8.5 Secure authentication"
Required Evidence: Identity configuration review; privileged-role export; conditional-access policy; authentication test results; recovery-process test
Success Criteria: Privileged identity paths and account recovery are protected by approved controls and monitored

Risk Scenario: Insufficient logs could delay incident detection and investigation
Proposed Treatment Actions: Define mandatory log sources and retention; synchronize system time; restrict log administration; monitor ingestion failures; test alerts for critical authentication and system events
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.8.15 Logging; A.8.16 Monitoring activities; A.8.17 Clock synchronization; A.5.24 Information security incident management planning and preparation"
Required Evidence: Logging coverage matrix; retention configuration; time-synchronization settings; ingestion-health dashboard; alert test records
Success Criteria: Critical in-scope systems generate searchable, time-aligned logs and alert tests produce documented results

Risk Scenario: Compromised development devices could expose credentials or source code
Proposed Treatment Actions: Apply endpoint protection and patching to development devices; restrict local administrator rights; separate development from production; scan build artifacts and dependencies; train developers on secure handling
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.8.7 Protection against malware; A.8.8 Management of technical vulnerabilities; A.8.25 Secure development life cycle; A.8.31 Separation of development
Success Criteria: Development endpoint compliance report; patch report; environment-separation diagram and rules; dependency scan results; developer access review
Residual Likelihood: Development endpoints meet baseline requirements and development access cannot directly bypass production controls

Risk Scenario: Compromise could disrupt the platform or expose sensitive information
Proposed Treatment Actions: Establish secure configuration baselines; disable unnecessary services and ports; review administrative access; scan configuration drift; apply approved hardening and change control
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.8.9 Configuration management; A.8.20 Network security; A.8.22 Segregation of networks; A.8.32 Change management"
Required Evidence: Approved hardening baseline; server configuration scans; exposed-service review; change records; remediation tickets
Success Criteria: Production systems conform to approved baselines or have documented, time-bound exceptions

Risk Scenario: Abuse of privileged accounts could enable large-scale data disclosure or alteration
Proposed Treatment Actions: Maintain a privileged-account inventory; use separate admin accounts; enforce MFA; grant just-in-time or time-limited privilege where feasible; review privileged activity and remove dormant accounts
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.8.2 Privileged access rights; A.5.16 Identity management; A.5.18 Access rights; A.8.15 Logging"
Required Evidence: Privileged-account inventory; approval records; MFA report; privileged activity logs; periodic recertification
Success Criteria: Every privileged account has an owner, approved purpose, strong authentication and reviewed activity

Risk Scenario: Missed contractual security obligations could cause disputes or financial loss
Proposed Treatment Actions: Create a register of security and privacy obligations; assign obligation owners; review new and renewed contracts; map requirements to internal controls; monitor due dates and exceptions
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.31 Legal
Target Date: regulatory and contractual requirements; A.5.32 Intellectual property rights; A.5.34 Privacy and protection of PII"
Residual Likelihood: Contractual obligations register; reviewed contract checklist; assigned owners; compliance review records; exception log
Residual Impact: Applicable security commitments are recorded, assigned and periodically reviewed with overdue actions escalated

Risk Scenario: Unauthorized disclosure could affect employees and create legal or reputational consequences
Proposed Treatment Actions: Classify employee records; restrict HR data access by role; review access periodically; log access to sensitive records; apply retention and secure disposal rules
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.12 Classification of information; A.5.15 Access control; A.5.18 Access rights; A.5.34 Privacy and protection of PII"
Required Evidence: Data classification record; HR access matrix; access-review sign-off; access logs; retention and disposal records
Success Criteria: Employee records are accessible only to approved roles and access is periodically reviewed

Risk Scenario: Exposure of findings could help attackers exploit known weaknesses
Proposed Treatment Actions: First identify and register the repository or system that stores vulnerability reports; then restrict access to named security and remediation personnel; classify reports; encrypt storage and transfer; review downloads and sharing
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.12 Classification of information; A.5.15 Access control; A.8.3 Information access restriction; A.8.12 Data leakage prevention"
Required Evidence: Confirmed asset record and owner; approved access list; storage configuration; classification label; access logs; sharing review
Success Criteria: A matching asset is added to the inventory before closure and vulnerability reports are restricted to authorized personnel

Risk Scenario: Stolen secrets could enable unauthorized access or data decryption
Proposed Treatment Actions: Use an approved secrets-management or key-management service; restrict key access; rotate credentials and keys based on policy and after suspected exposure; separate key administration; log key use and protect backups
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.17 Authentication information; A.8.2 Privileged access rights; A.8.24 Use of cryptography; A.8.15 Logging"
Required Evidence: Key inventory; key-management configuration; access policy; rotation records; key-use logs; recovery test
Success Criteria: Keys and secrets are not stored in plaintext repositories and access, rotation and recovery are controlled

Risk Scenario: Support tickets could expose personal information or confidential customer details
Proposed Treatment Actions: First identify and register the ticketing platform as an asset; restrict ticket access by role and customer assignment; redact sensitive data where feasible; log privileged access; define retention and secure deletion
ISO 27001:2022 Annex A References: "A.5.12 Classification of information; A.5.15 Access control; A.5.18 Access rights; A.5.34 Privacy and protection of PII; A.8.3 Information access restriction"
Required Evidence: Confirmed asset record and owner; ticketing-role matrix; sample redaction test; access logs; retention configuration
Success Criteria: A matching asset is added to the inventory before closure and ticket access is restricted to authorized support personnel
